title: Cheapest walk with color-switch surcharge
code:
import heapq


def min_cost_route(n, edges, s, t, switch_cost):
    if s == t:
        return 0

    # State graph:
    #   ids 0..n-1       : "hub" of node v (at v, free to pick any color next)
    #   ids n..          : (v, color) = at v, travelling on edges of `color`
    # Transitions:
    #   hub(v)   -> (v, c)   cost 0            (choose color for the next edge)
    #   (v, c)   -> hub(v)   cost switch_cost  (drop the current color)
    #   (u, c)   -> (v, c)   cost w            (traverse an edge of color c)
    ids = {}
    node_of = list(range(n))
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]

    def get(v, c):
        key = (v, c)
        i = ids.get(key)
        if i is None:
            i = len(node_of)
            ids[key] = i
            node_of.append(v)
            adj.append([(v, switch_cost)])   # (v, c) -> hub(v)
            adj[v].append((i, 0))            # hub(v) -> (v, c)
        return i

    for u, v, w, c in edges:
        a = get(u, c)
        b = get(v, c)
        if a != b:
            adj[a].append((b, w))
            adj[b].append((a, w))
        # a self-loop never helps, so it adds no transition

    INF = float("inf")
    dist = [INF] * len(node_of)
    dist[s] = 0                      # start at hub(s): first edge is free of switch charge
    heap = [(0, s)]

    while heap:
        d, x = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if d > dist[x]:
            continue
        if node_of[x] == t:          # any state located at t means we have arrived
            return d
        for y, w in adj[x]:
            nd = d + w
            if nd < dist[y]:
                dist[y] = nd
                heapq.heappush(heap, (nd, y))

    return -1

title: Palindrome insertions from a restricted alphabet
code:
def min_insertions(s, allowed):
    allowed = set(allowed)
    n = len(s)
    if n < 2:
        return 0

    INF = float("inf")
    can = [ch in allowed for ch in s]

    # dp[i][j] = min insertions to make s[i..j] a palindrome (INF if impossible).
    # Cells with i >= j stay 0 (empty / single-character substrings).
    dp = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]

    for i in range(n - 2, -1, -1):
        row = dp[i]
        below = dp[i + 1]
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            best = INF
            # Pair the two end characters with each other.
            if s[i] == s[j]:
                best = below[j - 1]
            # Mirror s[i] by inserting a copy of it to the right of s[j].
            if can[i]:
                cand = below[j] + 1
                if cand < best:
                    best = cand
            # Mirror s[j] by inserting a copy of it to the left of s[i].
            if can[j]:
                cand = row[j - 1] + 1
                if cand < best:
                    best = cand
            row[j] = best

    res = dp[0][n - 1]
    return -1 if res == INF else res

title: Smallest solution of congruences with non-coprime moduli
code:
def solve_congruences(pairs):
    """Return the smallest non-negative x with x % m == r % m for every (r, m).

    Moduli need not be pairwise coprime. Raises ValueError if the system is
    inconsistent. Returns 0 for an empty list.
    """

    def ext_gcd(a, b):
        # Returns (g, s, t) with a*s + b*t == g == gcd(a, b)
        old_r, r = a, b
        old_s, s = 1, 0
        old_t, t = 0, 1
        while r:
            q = old_r // r
            old_r, r = r, old_r - q * r
            old_s, s = s, old_s - q * s
            old_t, t = t, old_t - q * t
        return old_r, old_s, old_t

    x, M = 0, 1  # invariant: solutions so far are exactly x (mod M)
    for r, m in pairs:
        if m < 1:
            raise ValueError("modulus must be >= 1")
        r %= m

        g, p, _ = ext_gcd(M, m)      # M*p + m*q == g
        diff = r - x
        if diff % g != 0:
            raise ValueError("no solution: congruences are inconsistent")

        m_g = m // g
        # Need x + M*k ≡ r (mod m)  <=>  (M/g)*k ≡ diff/g (mod m/g),
        # and p is the inverse of M/g modulo m/g.
        k = (diff // g) * p % m_g

        x += M * k
        M *= m_g                     # M = lcm(M, m)
        x %= M

    return int(x)

title: Ledger balances drift by one cent

import re

# Digits, optionally followed by "." and 1-2 digits. [0-9] (not \d) so only ASCII
# digits match; used with fullmatch so nothing else (including a trailing
# newline) is tolerated.
_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"([0-9]+)(?:\.([0-9]{1,2}))?")


def compute_balances(transactions):
    balances = {}
    for tx in transactions:
        amount = tx["amount"]
        match = _AMOUNT_RE.fullmatch(amount) if isinstance(amount, str) else None
        if match is None:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid amount: {amount!r}")

        whole, frac = match.groups()
        # Exact integer arithmetic: "0.5" -> 50, "0.29" -> 29, "7" -> 700.
        cents = int(whole) * 100 + (int(frac.ljust(2, "0")) if frac else 0)
        if cents <= 0:
            raise ValueError("amount must be positive")

        balances[tx["from"]] = balances.get(tx["from"], 0) - cents
        balances[tx["to"]] = balances.get(tx["to"], 0) + cents
    return balances

    if start >= end:
        raise ValueError("empty booking")

    # Bookings that end at or before the new start do not overlap it.

        result.append(bookings[i])
        i += 1
    # Only bookings that start strictly before the new end overlap it.
    while i < len(bookings) and bookings[i][0] < end:

        end = max(end, bookings[i][1])

    result.append((start, end))

code:
from collections import OrderedDict
import heapq


class TTLCache:
    """Fixed-capacity LRU cache with optional per-entry TTL, driven by an
    explicit logical clock, with operation statistics."""

    def __init__(self, capacity):
        if isinstance(capacity, bool) or not isinstance(capacity, int) or capacity < 1:
            raise ValueError("capacity must be an integer >= 1")
        self._capacity = capacity
        # key -> [value, expires_at (or None), token]; order = LRU -> MRU
        self._data = OrderedDict()
        # min-heap of (expires_at, token, key); stale records are skipped lazily
        self._heap = []
        self._token = 0
        self._hits = 0
        self._misses = 0
        self._evictions = 0
        self._expirations = 0

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ internals

    def _purge(self, now):
        """Remove every stored entry that is dead at `now`."""
        heap = self._heap
        data = self._data
        while heap and heap[0][0] <= now:
            _, token, key = heapq.heappop(heap)
            entry = data.get(key)
            # Only act if this heap record describes the entry's current state
            if entry is not None and entry[2] == token:
                del data[key]
                self._expirations += 1

    def _compact_heap_if_needed(self):
        """Drop stale heap records so the heap stays O(len(cache))."""
        if len(self._heap) > 2 * len(self._data) + 16:
            self._heap = [
                (entry[1], entry[2], key)
                for key, entry in self._data.items()
                if entry[1] is not None
            ]
            heapq.heapify(self._heap)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ public API

    def put(self, key, value, now, ttl=None):
        if ttl is not None and not (ttl > 0):
            raise ValueError("ttl must be None or a positive number")

        self._purge(now)

        expires_at = None if ttl is None else now + ttl
        self._token += 1
        token = self._token

        data = self._data
        if key in data:
            # Update: never an eviction
            entry = data[key]
            entry[0] = value
            entry[1] = expires_at
            entry[2] = token  # invalidates any older heap record
            data.move_to_end(key)
        else:
            if len(data) >= self._capacity:
                data.popitem(last=False)  # least-recently-used
                self._evictions += 1
            data[key] = [value, expires_at, token]

        if expires_at is not None:
            heapq.heappush(self._heap, (expires_at, token, key))
        self._compact_heap_if_needed()

    def get(self, key, now):
        self._purge(now)
        entry = self._data.get(key)
        if entry is None:
            self._misses += 1
            return None
        self._hits += 1
        self._data.move_to_end(key)
        return entry[0]

    def stats(self):
        return {
            "hits": self._hits,
            "misses": self._misses,
            "evictions": self._evictions,
            "expirations": self._expirations,
        }

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self._data)

title: Mergeable component ledger with undo
code:
class MergeLedger:
    """Partition of labeled elements with merge, LIFO undo of merges,
    and per-component size / value aggregates.

    A union-find forest with union by size and no path compression, so
    every merge is one parent link that can be removed again. Trees have
    depth O(log n). Each node stores the size and value sum of its own
    subtree, so detaching a child on undo only needs to subtract the
    child's current subtree aggregates from the root.
    """

    _ROOT = object()  # parent marker for roots (labels may be None)

    def __init__(self):
        self._parent = {}   # label -> parent label, or _ROOT
        self._size = {}     # label -> number of elements in its subtree
        self._sum = {}      # label -> sum of values in its subtree
        self._value = {}    # label -> the element's own value
        self._touch = {}    # label -> number of add_value calls passing through
        self._history = []  # stack of merge records
        self._components = 0

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ internals

    def _find(self, x):
        parent = self._parent
        if x not in parent:
            raise KeyError(x)
        root_marker = self._ROOT
        while True:
            p = parent[x]
            if p is root_marker:
                return x
            x = p

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- mutation

    def add(self, x, value=0):
        if x in self._parent:
            raise ValueError(f"element already exists: {x!r}")
        self._parent[x] = self._ROOT
        self._size[x] = 1
        self._sum[x] = value
        self._value[x] = value
        self._touch[x] = 0
        self._components += 1

    def merge(self, a, b):
        ra = self._find(a)
        rb = self._find(b)          # both validated before any change
        if ra is rb or ra == rb:
            return False
        if self._size[ra] < self._size[rb]:
            ra, rb = rb, ra         # ra = larger tree, stays root
        # Remember the root's sum before the merge and the touch counters,
        # so undo can restore the sum exactly when the root's side was not
        # modified in the meantime (avoids float round-off from a+b-b).
        self._history.append(
            (rb, ra, self._sum[ra], self._touch[ra], self._touch[rb])
        )
        self._parent[rb] = ra
        self._size[ra] += self._size[rb]
        self._sum[ra] = self._sum[ra] + self._sum[rb]
        self._components += 1 - 2  # two components became one
        return True

    def undo(self):
        if not self._history:
            raise RuntimeError("no merge to undo")
        child, root, root_sum_before, root_touch, child_touch = self._history.pop()
        # All later merges are already undone, so `root` is a root again
        # and `child` is still its direct child.
        self._parent[child] = self._ROOT
        self._size[root] -= self._size[child]
        touched_root = self._touch[root] - root_touch
        touched_child = self._touch[child] - child_touch
        if touched_root == touched_child:
            # Every value change that reached the root came through the
            # child's subtree, so the root's side is unchanged.
            self._sum[root] = root_sum_before
        else:
            self._sum[root] = self._sum[root] - self._sum[child]
        self._components += 1

    def add_value(self, x, delta):
        parent = self._parent
        if x not in parent:
            raise KeyError(x)
        self._value[x] = self._value[x] + delta
        sums, touch, root_marker = self._sum, self._touch, self._ROOT
        node = x
        while node is not root_marker:   # update every ancestor's subtree sum
            sums[node] = sums[node] + delta
            touch[node] += 1
            node = parent[node]

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- queries

    def same(self, a, b):
        ra = self._find(a)
        rb = self._find(b)
        return ra is rb or ra == rb

    def component_size(self, x):
        return self._size[self._find(x)]

    def component_value(self, x):
        return self._sum[self._find(x)]

    def components(self):
        return self._components

title: Normalized integer interval set

from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right


class IntervalSet:
    """A set of integers stored as sorted, disjoint, non-adjacent
    half-open intervals [lo, hi)."""

    def __init__(self):
        # Parallel sorted arrays: interval k is [self._starts[k], self._ends[k]).
        # Invariant: starts[k] < ends[k] < starts[k+1]  (strict => non-adjacent).
        self._starts = []
        self._ends = []

    @staticmethod
    def _check(lo, hi):
        if lo >= hi:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid interval [{lo}, {hi}): require lo < hi")

    def add(self, lo, hi):
        self._check(lo, hi)
        starts, ends = self._starts, self._ends
        # Intervals that overlap OR touch [lo, hi): end >= lo and start <= hi.
        i = bisect_left(ends, lo)      # first interval with end >= lo
        j = bisect_right(starts, hi)   # first interval with start > hi
        if i < j:
            lo = min(lo, starts[i])
            hi = max(hi, ends[j - 1])
        starts[i:j] = [lo]
        ends[i:j] = [hi]

    def remove(self, lo, hi):
        self._check(lo, hi)
        starts, ends = self._starts, self._ends
        # Intervals that strictly overlap [lo, hi): end > lo and start < hi.
        i = bisect_right(ends, lo)     # first interval with end > lo
        j = bisect_left(starts, hi)    # first interval with start >= hi
        if i >= j:
            return
        new_starts, new_ends = [], []
        if starts[i] < lo:             # left remnant survives
            new_starts.append(starts[i])
            new_ends.append(lo)
        if ends[j - 1] > hi:           # right remnant survives
            new_starts.append(hi)
            new_ends.append(ends[j - 1])
        starts[i:j] = new_starts
        ends[i:j] = new_ends

    def contains(self, x):
        k = bisect_right(self._starts, x) - 1   # last interval with start <= x
        return k >= 0 and x < self._ends[k]

    def total(self):
        return sum(e - s for s, e in zip(self._starts, self._ends))

    def intervals(self):
        return list(zip(self._starts, self._ends))

    def gaps(self, lo, hi):
        self._check(lo, hi)
        starts, ends = self._starts, self._ends
        i = bisect_right(ends, lo)     # first interval with end > lo
        j = bisect_left(starts, hi)    # first interval with start >= hi
        result = []
        cur = lo
        for k in range(i, j):
            if starts[k] > cur:
                result.append((cur, starts[k]))
            cur = ends[k]
        if cur < hi:
            result.append((cur, hi))
        return result

title: Reprioritizable task scheduler with FIFO ties
code:
import heapq


class TaskScheduler:
    """Priority queue of unique task ids with reprioritization and cancellation.

    Higher priority is served first; ties are broken by original submission
    order (FIFO). All operations are O(log n) amortized.

    Implementation: a binary heap with lazy deletion. Each heap entry is
    (-priority, seq, token, task_id), where
      * seq   -- FIFO position, assigned at submission, kept on reprioritize
      * token -- unique per heap entry; an entry is live only if its token
                 matches the one recorded for the task in `_active`.
    Stale entries (from reprioritize / cancel) are skipped when they surface
    at the top, and the heap is rebuilt when stale entries outnumber live ones.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._heap = []      # (-priority, seq, token, task_id)
        self._active = {}    # task_id -> (priority, seq, token)
        self._next_seq = 0
        self._next_token = 0

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ internals

    def _push(self, task_id, priority, seq):
        token = self._next_token
        self._next_token += 1
        self._active[task_id] = (priority, seq, token)
        # token is unique, so tuple comparison never reaches task_id
        heapq.heappush(self._heap, (-priority, seq, token, task_id))

    def _prune_top(self):
        """Discard stale entries sitting on top of the heap."""
        heap, active = self._heap, self._active
        while heap:
            _, _, token, task_id = heap[0]
            rec = active.get(task_id)
            if rec is not None and rec[2] == token:
                return
            heapq.heappop(heap)

    def _maybe_compact(self):
        """Rebuild the heap if it is dominated by stale entries."""
        if len(self._heap) > 2 * len(self._active) + 16:
            self._heap = [
                (-priority, seq, token, task_id)
                for task_id, (priority, seq, token) in self._active.items()
            ]
            heapq.heapify(self._heap)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ public API

    def submit(self, task_id, priority):
        if task_id in self._active:
            raise ValueError(f"task {task_id!r} is already active")
        seq = self._next_seq
        self._next_seq += 1
        self._push(task_id, priority, seq)

    def reprioritize(self, task_id, priority):
        rec = self._active.get(task_id)
        if rec is None:
            raise KeyError(task_id)
        old_priority, seq, _ = rec
        if priority == old_priority:
            return  # nothing changes; FIFO position is preserved
        # New entry with the ORIGINAL seq; the old entry becomes stale
        # because its token no longer matches.
        self._push(task_id, priority, seq)
        self._maybe_compact()

    def cancel(self, task_id):
        if task_id not in self._active:
            raise KeyError(task_id)
        del self._active[task_id]   # heap entry becomes stale
        self._maybe_compact()

    def pop(self):
        self._prune_top()
        if not self._heap:
            raise IndexError("pop from empty TaskScheduler")
        _, _, _, task_id = heapq.heappop(self._heap)
        del self._active[task_id]
        return task_id

    def peek(self):
        self._prune_top()
        if not self._heap:
            raise IndexError("peek at empty TaskScheduler")
        return self._heap[0][3]

    def priority_of(self, task_id):
        rec = self._active.get(task_id)
        if rec is None:
            raise KeyError(task_id)
        return rec[0]

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self._active)

title: Display-width truncation with combining marks
code:
import unicodedata

_COMBINING_CATEGORIES = frozenset(("Mn", "Mc", "Me"))


def truncate_display(s: str, width: int) -> str:
    """Truncate `s` to at most `width` display units.

    A unit is a non-combining code point together with all combining marks
    (categories Mn, Mc, Me) that immediately follow it. If the string starts
    with combining marks, that leading run forms one unit on its own.
    Units are never split.
    """
    if width < 0:
        raise ValueError("width must be non-negative")

    units = 0
    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
        # A new unit starts at the very first code point (even if it is a
        # combining mark with nothing to attach to) and at every
        # non-combining code point.
        starts_unit = i == 0 or unicodedata.category(ch) not in _COMBINING_CATEGORIES
        if starts_unit:
            if units == width:
                # We already have `width` whole units; cut before this one.
                return s[:i]
            units += 1

    # Fewer than or exactly `width` units in total: return unchanged.
    return s

title: Even chunking of arbitrary iterables

from operator import index


def chunk_evenly(items, n: int) -> list[list]:
    """Split `items` into exactly `n` contiguous chunks whose lengths differ by at most 1.

    The first L % n chunks have L // n + 1 elements and the rest have L // n,
    where L is the total number of elements. If there are fewer than n
    elements, the trailing chunks are empty lists.

    Raises ValueError if n < 1.
    """
    n = index(n)  # rejects non-integers (e.g. floats) with TypeError
    if n < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"n must be at least 1, got {n}")

    data = list(items)  # consume the iterable exactly once
    base, extra = divmod(len(data), n)

    chunks = []
    start = 0
    for i in range(n):
        size = base + 1 if i < extra else base
        chunks.append(data[start:start + size])
        start += size
    return chunks

def kth_root_floor(n: int, k: int) -> int:
    """Return the largest integer r >= 0 such that r ** k <= n.

    Uses only integer arithmetic, so the result is exact for arbitrarily
    large n. Raises ValueError if n < 0 or k < 1.
    """
    if n < 0 or k < 1:
        raise ValueError("n must be >= 0 and k must be >= 1")

    if n < 2 or k == 1:
        return n

    bits = n.bit_length()

    # n < 2**bits <= 2**k whenever k >= bits, so the root is 1.
    if k >= bits:
        return 1

    # Initial guess r = 2**ceil(bits / k), which is >= the true root,
    # because r**k >= 2**bits > n.
    r = 1 << -(-bits // k)

    # Integer Newton iteration, decreasing monotonically from above.
    # While r**k > n the next iterate is strictly smaller, and by AM-GM
    # it never drops below floor(n ** (1/k)). So the first time the
    # iterate fails to decrease, r is the answer.
    km1 = k - 1
    while True:
        t = (km1 * r + n // r ** km1) // k
        if t >= r:
            return r
        r = t

title: Largest-remainder integer allocation
code:
from fractions import Fraction
from operator import index


def allocate_shares(total: int, weights: list) -> list[int]:
    """Split `total` into integer shares proportional to `weights` using the
    largest-remainder method; remainder ties go to the lower index.

    All arithmetic is exact (Fractions), so float rounding can never
    mis-order remainders or make the result sum to anything but `total`.
    """
    total = index(total)  # accepts int-like values, rejects floats (TypeError)
    if total < 0:
        raise ValueError("total must be >= 0")
    if len(weights) == 0:
        raise ValueError("weights must be non-empty")

    try:
        w = [Fraction(x) for x in weights]  # exact, even for floats/Decimals
    except OverflowError:  # infinite weight
        raise ValueError("weights must be finite numbers") from None
    # (NaN weights already raise ValueError inside Fraction())

    if any(x < 0 for x in w):
        raise ValueError("weights must be >= 0")
    W = sum(w)
    if W == 0:
        raise ValueError("sum of weights must be > 0")

    quotas = [total * x / W for x in w]
    shares = [q.numerator // q.denominator for q in quotas]  # floor(q_i)
    remainders = [q - s for q, s in zip(quotas, shares)]

    leftover = total - sum(shares)  # 0 <= leftover < len(weights)
    order = sorted(range(len(w)), key=lambda i: (-remainders[i], i))
    for i in order[:leftover]:
        shares[i] += 1

    return shares

title: Lazy round-robin interleaver
code:
def round_robin(iterables: list) -> "iterator":
    """Lazily interleave values from a list of iterables.

    Yields the first item of each iterable in list order, then the second
    item of each, and so on. Exhausted iterables drop out of the rotation;
    the rest keep their original relative order.

    Inputs are never materialized and are advanced only as far as needed to
    produce the values actually requested, so unbounded inputs are fine.
    """
    # iter() only obtains an iterator; it does not consume any items.
    iterators = [iter(it) for it in iterables]

    def _rotate(active):
        while active:
            still_active = []
            for it in active:
                try:
                    value = next(it)
                except StopIteration:
                    # Exhausted: drop it from the rotation and never touch it again.
                    continue
                still_active.append(it)
                yield value
            active = still_active

    return _rotate(iterators)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import itertools

    assert list(round_robin([[1, 2, 3], "ab", [10]])) == [1, "a", 10, 2, "b", 3]
    assert list(round_robin([[], [1, 2], []])) == [1, 2]
    assert list(round_robin([])) == []
    assert list(round_robin([[], "", ()])) == []
    assert list(
        itertools.islice(round_robin([itertools.count(0), itertools.count(100)]), 4)
    ) == [0, 100, 1, 101]

    # Laziness check: inputs must not be advanced beyond what was requested.
    def guarded(limit):
        for i in range(limit):
            yield i
        raise AssertionError("over-advanced")

    rr = round_robin([guarded(2), guarded(2)])
    assert iter(rr) is rr
    assert [next(rr) for _ in range(4)] == [0, 0, 1, 1]
    print("ok")

title: Lower weighted median with tolerance

import math


def weighted_median(values: list, weights: list) -> float:
    if len(values) != len(weights):
        raise ValueError("values and weights must have the same length")
    if len(values) == 0:
        raise ValueError("values must not be empty")

    for w in weights:
        # `not (w >= 0)` also rejects NaN weights
        if not (w >= 0):
            raise ValueError("weights must be non-negative")

    # Drop zero-weight entries: they contribute nothing and must never be
    # returned merely because the tolerance makes the threshold <= 0
    # (e.g. when the total weight is tiny).
    pairs = [(v, w) for v, w in zip(values, weights) if w > 0]
    if not pairs:
        raise ValueError("total weight must be positive")

    pairs.sort(key=lambda p: p[0])

    total = math.fsum(w for _, w in pairs)
    threshold = total / 2 - 1e-9

    cumulative = 0.0
    for v, w in pairs:
        cumulative += w
        if cumulative >= threshold:
            return v

    # Unreachable in practice (cumulative ends at ~total >= threshold),
    # but guard against floating-point oddities.
    return pairs[-1][0]

title: Overflow-safe Euclidean norm
code:
import math
import sys
from fractions import Fraction


def vector_norm(v: list[float]) -> float:
    """Euclidean (L2) norm of v, robust across the full double-precision range.

    Raises ValueError if any entry is NaN or +/-infinity.
    """
    xs = [float(x) for x in v]
    for x in xs:
        if not math.isfinite(x):
            raise ValueError("vector_norm: entries must be finite (got %r)" % (x,))

    m = max((abs(x) for x in xs), default=0.0)
    if m == 0.0:
        return 0.0  # empty or all-zero vector

    # Scale by a power of two so the largest entry lands in [0.5, 1).
    # Power-of-two scaling is exact, so it adds no rounding error; entries
    # that underflow during scaling are < 2**-1000 times the largest one
    # and cannot affect the result.
    _, e = math.frexp(m)
    total = math.fsum(math.ldexp(x, -e) ** 2 for x in xs)  # in [0.25, n)
    r = math.sqrt(total)

    try:
        return math.ldexp(r, e)  # undo the scaling (exact unless subnormal)
    except OverflowError:
        # The result does not fit in a double. Usually the true norm really
        # exceeds the largest float, but it could sit a hair below it with
        # rounding pushing us over. Settle this rare case exactly.
        fmax = sys.float_info.max
        exact_sq = sum(Fraction(x) ** 2 for x in xs)
        if exact_sq <= Fraction(fmax) ** 2:
            return fmax  # true norm is within ~1 ulp of the largest float
        return math.inf  # true norm is not representable as a finite float

import heapq


def max_bounty(jobs: list[tuple[int, int]], cap: int) -> int:
    if cap < 1:
        raise ValueError("cap must be at least 1")
    if not jobs:
        return 0

    heap: list[int] = []          # min-heap of bounties of currently kept jobs
    push = heapq.heappush
    replace = heapq.heapreplace
    size = 0

    for d, p in sorted(jobs):     # ascending deadline
        if size < cap * d:        # still room in slots 1..d
            push(heap, p)
            size += 1
        elif p > heap[0]:         # full: swap out the cheapest kept job
            replace(heap, p)

    return sum(heap)

from itertools import accumulate


def count_pulses(deltas: list[int], k: int, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    n = len(deltas)
    if not (1 <= lo <= hi <= n):
        raise ValueError(
            "lo and hi must satisfy 1 <= lo <= hi <= len(deltas)"
        )

    # Prefix sums P[0..n]; subarray (i, j] has sum P[j] - P[i], which is a
    # multiple of k  <=>  P[i] % k == P[j] % k  (Python's % is non-negative
    # for positive k, so negative sums are handled correctly).
    #
    # Compress each residue to a small integer id so the sliding-window
    # counts can live in a flat list instead of a dict.
    ids = {}
    setdefault = ids.setdefault
    ident = [setdefault(p % k, len(ids)) for p in accumulate(deltas, initial=0)]
    cnt = [0] * len(ids)

    total = 0

    # For each right end j (lo <= j <= n) the valid left ends are
    # i in [max(0, j - hi), j - lo].  Maintain counts of residues in that
    # window and add the number of matches for P[j].

    # Phase 1: j = lo .. hi  -> window only grows (i = j - lo enters).
    for a, c in zip(ident[0:hi - lo + 1], ident[lo:hi + 1]):
        cnt[a] += 1
        total += cnt[c]

    # Phase 2: j = hi+1 .. n -> i = j - lo enters, i = j - hi - 1 leaves.
    for a, b, c in zip(ident[hi + 1 - lo:n - lo + 1],
                       ident[0:n - hi],
                       ident[hi + 1:n + 1]):
        cnt[a] += 1
        cnt[b] -= 1
        total += cnt[c]

    return total

def longest_echo(s: str) -> int:
    """Length of the longest substring of s occurring at least twice
    (occurrences may overlap). Returns 0 if there is none."""
    if len(s) < 2:
        return 0

    # Suffix automaton: per-state transition dict, suffix link, and
    # length of the longest substring in that state.
    nxt = [{}]
    link = [-1]
    length = [0]
    last = 0

    for ch in s:
        cur = len(length)
        length.append(length[last] + 1)
        nxt.append({})
        link.append(0)

        p = last
        while p != -1:
            trans = nxt[p]
            if ch in trans:
                break
            trans[ch] = cur
            p = link[p]

        if p != -1:
            q = nxt[p][ch]
            if length[p] + 1 == length[q]:
                link[cur] = q
            else:
                clone = len(length)
                length.append(length[p] + 1)
                nxt.append(nxt[q].copy())
                link.append(link[q])
                while p != -1:
                    trans = nxt[p]
                    if trans.get(ch) != q:
                        break
                    trans[ch] = clone
                    p = link[p]
                link[q] = clone
                link[cur] = clone
        # else: link[cur] stays 0 (the root)

        last = cur

    # A state's substrings occur >= 2 times exactly when the state has a
    # child in the suffix-link tree. So the answer is the largest length
    # among states that are some other state's suffix link.
    best = 0
    for v in range(1, len(length)):
        l = length[link[v]]
        if l > best:
            best = l
    return best

from collections import Counter


def count_locked_pairs(values: list[int], m: int) -> int:
    if m < 1:
        raise ValueError("m must be >= 1")

    # Fold the parity condition into the modulus:
    #  - m even: a sum divisible by m is even, so the two values
    #    automatically share parity -> condition is sum % m == 0.
    #  - m odd:  "sum divisible by m" and "sum even" together are equivalent
    #    to sum % (2m) == 0 (since gcd(m, 2) == 1).
    M = m if m % 2 == 0 else 2 * m

    # Python's % with a positive modulus always yields a value in [0, M),
    # so negative inputs are handled correctly.
    counts = Counter([v % M for v in values])

    total = 0
    get = counts.get
    for r, c in counts.items():
        s = (M - r) % M          # complementary residue
        if s == r:               # r == 0, or r == M/2 when M is even
            total += c * (c - 1) // 2
        elif r < s:              # count each complementary pair of classes once
            total += c * get(s, 0)
    return total

def peak_load(intervals: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    # The load only increases at interval start times, so the maximum load
    # is always first attained at some start. Sweep over the sorted starts,
    # retiring every interval whose end is <= the current start (half-open
    # ranges: an interval ending at t is not active at t).
    starts = sorted(s for s, _ in intervals)
    ends = sorted(e for _, e in intervals)

    j = 0          # index of the next end not yet retired
    cur = 0        # current load
    best = 0
    best_t = 0

    for s in starts:
        # ends[j] <= s can never run out of bounds: the interval that
        # starts at s has an end > s, so at least one end remains.
        while ends[j] <= s:
            j += 1
            cur -= 1
        cur += 1
        if cur > best:      # strict '>' keeps the earliest time
            best = cur
            best_t = s

    return best, best_t

def recurring_counts(data: list[int], queries: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[int]:
    n = len(data)
    q = len(queries)
    res = [0] * q
    if n == 0 or q == 0:
        return res

    # Process queries in order of right endpoint.
    order = sorted(range(q), key=lambda k: queries[k][1])
    qi = 0

    tree = [0] * (n + 1)   # Fenwick tree over positions (1-based internally)
    last = {}              # value -> most recent position seen
    prev = [-1] * n        # prev[i] = previous position holding data[i], or -1
    active = 0             # number of marks = values seen at least twice so far

    for i in range(n + 1):
        # Answer all queries with r == i (positions 0..i-1 have been processed).
        while qi < q:
            k = order[qi]
            l, r = queries[k]
            if r != i:
                break
            # marks at positions < l
            s = 0
            j = l
            while j > 0:
                s += tree[j]
                j &= j - 1
            res[k] = active - s
            qi += 1

        if i == n:
            break

        # Add position i to the processed prefix.
        v = data[i]
        p = last.get(v)
        if p is not None:
            prev[i] = p
            # New second-to-last occurrence is p: place the mark there.
            j = p + 1
            while j <= n:
                tree[j] += 1
                j += j & -j
            pp = prev[p]
            if pp >= 0:
                # Remove the old mark (previous second-to-last occurrence).
                j = pp + 1
                while j <= n:
                    tree[j] -= 1
                    j += j & -j
            else:
                active += 1   # value has just become "recurring"
        last[v] = i

    return res

from collections import deque


def count_stable_windows(readings: list[int], tol: int) -> int:
    """Count non-empty contiguous subarrays with max - min <= tol.

    Sliding window with two monotonic deques: O(n) time, O(n) memory.
    """
    max_dq = deque()  # indices; values strictly decreasing -> front is window max
    min_dq = deque()  # indices; values strictly increasing -> front is window min
    left = 0          # smallest valid start for the current right end
    total = 0

    for right, v in enumerate(readings):
        # Maintain monotonic deques with the new element.
        while max_dq and readings[max_dq[-1]] <= v:
            max_dq.pop()
        max_dq.append(right)

        while min_dq and readings[min_dq[-1]] >= v:
            min_dq.pop()
        min_dq.append(right)

        # Shrink from the left until the window is stable again.
        # The window must start after whichever extreme occurs earlier.
        while readings[max_dq[0]] - readings[min_dq[0]] > tol:
            if max_dq[0] < min_dq[0]:
                left = max_dq.popleft() + 1
            else:
                left = min_dq.popleft() + 1

        # Every start in [left, right] gives a stable window ending at `right`.
        total += right - left + 1

    return total

from bisect import bisect_right


def count_dominant_pairs(seq: list[int]) -> int:
    """Count pairs (i, j), i < j, with seq[i] > 3 * seq[j] (exact, strict)."""
    n = len(seq)
    if n < 2:
        return 0

    # Coordinate-compress the values.
    vals = sorted(set(seq))
    m = len(vals)
    rank = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(vals)}  # 1-based ranks

    tree = [0] * (m + 1)  # Fenwick tree over ranks: counts of elements seen so far
    total = 0

    for seen, x in enumerate(seq):
        # Number of distinct values <= 3*x; earlier elements with rank <= k
        # are those that do NOT satisfy seq[i] > 3*x.
        k = bisect_right(vals, 3 * x)
        not_greater = 0
        while k:
            not_greater += tree[k]
            k &= k - 1
        total += seen - not_greater

        # Insert x into the tree (after querying, so that i < j strictly).
        i = rank[x]
        while i <= m:
            tree[i] += 1
            i += i & -i

    return total

title: Depth-limited flatten, iteration only
code:
def flatten_depth(nested, max_depth):
    if not isinstance(nested, list):
        raise TypeError("nested must be a list")
    if isinstance(max_depth, bool) or not isinstance(max_depth, int):
        raise TypeError("max_depth must be an int")
    if max_depth < 0:
        raise ValueError("max_depth must be >= 0")

    result = []
    # Explicit stack of iterators; len(stack) - 1 is the depth of the
    # list currently being walked (0 for the top-level list).
    stack = [iter(nested)]

    while stack:
        current = stack[-1]
        depth = len(stack) - 1
        descended = False

        for item in current:
            if depth < max_depth and isinstance(item, list):
                # Descend into this sub-list; the parent iterator stays on
                # the stack and resumes where it left off afterwards.
                stack.append(iter(item))
                descended = True
                break
            result.append(item)

        if not descended:
            # Current list exhausted.
            stack.pop()

    return result

title: Duration string parser under a no-import contract
code:
def parse_duration(text):
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise TypeError("expected str, got " + type(text).__name__)

    if str.strip(text) == "":
        raise ValueError("empty duration")

    order = "hms"
    multipliers = (3600, 60, 1)

    total = 0
    value = 0
    have_digits = False
    next_unit = 0  # index in `order` of the earliest unit still allowed

    for ch in text:
        if "0" <= ch <= "9":
            value = value * 10 + (ord(ch) - 48)
            have_digits = True
            continue

        idx = order.find(ch)
        # idx == -1 -> unknown character (whitespace, sign, uppercase, '.', ...)
        # idx < next_unit -> out of order or repeated component
        # not have_digits -> unit letter with no digits before it
        if idx < next_unit or not have_digits:
            raise ValueError("malformed duration: %r" % (text,))

        total += value * multipliers[idx]
        next_unit = idx + 1
        value = 0
        have_digits = False

    # Trailing digits with no unit letter
    if have_digits:
        raise ValueError("malformed duration: %r" % (text,))

    return total
